business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Investment Chapter of the Korea-United States Free Trade Agreement (KORUS FTA)

Convention between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), as amended, with its Enforcement Decree and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) examination manual; Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (FSCMA), including public-disclosure provisions for listed SPAC issuers; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations; Commercial Act and Commercial Registration Act; Financial Services Commission Beneficial Ownership Identification and Verification Guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Incorporation of Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean district court registry operated under the Supreme Court of Korea, accessible through i-ROS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: document authentication and Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Consular legalization route: notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then legalization by the destination embassy or consulate for non-Apostille states. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Registered Corporate Information attesting existence, directors and registered address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office / competent Korean district court registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: court-certified extract followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Consular legalization route: court-certified extract, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then consular legalization by the destination state. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation service provider and foreign filing agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / founding shareholders of the proposed Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: Korean notarization of the resolution, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Consular legalization route: Korean notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then consular legalization by the destination embassy or consulate. The two paths are mutually exclusive and sequential chaining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Articles of Incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarized Articles of Association, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Consular legalization route: notarized Articles, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then consular legalization by the destination state. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be used sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the proposed corporate banking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank with corporate customer due diligence records (e.g., Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Woori Bank or Hana Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: bank compliance officer signature notarized by a Korean notary, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Consular legalization route: notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then consular legalization by the destination state. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and never chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened before incorporation against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Korean FIU sanctions list under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and additional domestic enforcement notices. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence: board-approved acceptance, documented source of wealth and funds, enhanced transaction monitoring, annual rescreening, and escalation of any name-similarity hit to the AML compliance committee before filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-ROS) company name search module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered name must be written in Korean script and must contain the statutory corporate-form suffix Chusik Hoesa. An optional English name for cross-border documents must follow a phonetic transliteration consistent with the Revised Romanization of Korean unless the entity is a listed SPAC and a distinct English title is separately registered with the Financial Supervisory Service. The name structure follows a four-tier hierarchy: distinctive trade denomination, business-object description, legal-form suffix, and optional transliterated English title. The registry rejects names that are identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An extension is not available; if the name clearance expires, the applicant must submit a fresh clearance search. Within 14 days of receiving a name-rejection notice, the applicant must file a written appeal with the head of the competent district court registry, annexing the rejected name, the registry's stated grounds, proposed amended names, and a legal opinion on non-confusing use. The registry must issue a reasoned decision within 7 business days. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may apply to the competent district court for review under the Commercial Registration Act, and may appeal that decision to the relevant High Court within 14 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a SPAC listing vehicle, a virtual office or commercial mail-drop is impermissible before and after listing. Korean tax, banking and capital-markets practice require a physical registered address that is staffed, supported by an executed commercial lease, local signage, utility contracts, and actual custody of statutory records and financial books. The National Tax Service, Financial Services Commission and commercial banks will reject a virtual address because it cannot satisfy place-of-business verification and customer due diligence. The Chusik Hoesa must maintain core corporate records in Korea and be prepared for unannounced examination.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection: executed commercial lease in corporate name, physical signage, staffed desks during business hours, utility contracts, business license on display, original statutory registers and board minute book, accounting system with electronic vouchers, and records/mailbox capacity. Quantified risk: High; approximately 85% probability of a physical compliance visit by the Supreme Court registry, National Tax Service or Financial Services Commission within the first 18 months for a SPAC/blank-check medium-risk entity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean corporate name clearance and i-ROS certified search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-ROS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory i-ROS electronic filing tariff plus official certified extract fees; no attorney component.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chusik Hoesa incorporation registration fee and capital registration tax
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean court registry and competent local tax office under the National Tax Service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Capital Registration Tax under the Local Tax Act at 0.4% of paid-in capital plus 0.2% local education surtax, combined with the court filing fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of five-document mandatory bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean notary public, Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Section, and, if required, foreign embassy or consulate in Seoul
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean notarial tariff, Ministry of Foreign Affairs per-document Apostille fee, and prevailing foreign consular legalization fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External licensed Korean legal counsel and KoFIU-registered AML compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark hourly rate of USD 250-350 per hour for senior cross-border and AML counsel.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office provisioning and first-year commercial substance setup for SPAC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord and approved local physical office facility provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark lease for a staffed grade-B office in Seoul or Incheon, including signage, records room, utility contracts and first-year occupancy.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter and corporate banking pre-onboarding due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank and external counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published customer due diligence and reference-letter fee, plus external counsel document review at prevailing market rate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), especially Articles 288, 289, 291-295, 317, 329-331, 337, 389, 393 and 434; Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (Act No. 8635, as amended), Articles 6, 9, 119-128 and 180; Korea Exchange KOSDAQ Listing Rules and specialized SPAC regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court Registration Office for a registered office in Seoul; otherwise the District Court Registration Office with jurisdiction over the Company's principal place of business in the Republic of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company submitted together with notarized Articles of Incorporation, share subscription payment certificates, director and statutory auditor acceptance documents, corporate seal selection notice, and related incorporation meeting minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, to qualify as a Special Purpose Acquisition Company, or SPAC, under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act and the Korea Exchange KOSDAQ Listing Rules, the Company must maintain at least KRW 3,000,000,000 in paid-in capital at the time of the public offering, and at least 90 percent of the gross proceeds collected in the initial public offering must be deposited into an independent trust or escrow account maintained with a licensed Korean financial institution. The escrowed proceeds may be released only upon consummation of an approved business combination or redemption event, pursuant to the trust agreement and applicable capital markets regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
THE PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [SPAC] CO., LTD. (the "COMPANY")

WHEREAS the Company has been duly incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea on [Date], with authorized share capital of [total authorized shares] shares and issued shares of [issued shares] shares;

WHEREAS the underwriting sponsor, in connection with the Special Purpose Acquisition Company ("SPAC") structure, has subscribed for and fully paid the initial subscription price into the Company's designated payment account, and the board is required to ratify all capital subscription transactions;

WHEREAS the board is empowered by Article 393 of the Commercial Act to resolve corporate transactions and operations, and is required to appoint statutory officers whose names must be registered in the corporate registry;

WHEREAS the Company intends to adopt a principal place of business at [registered office address] for use as its registered office under Article 288 of the Commercial Act and to open banking and escrow accounts.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that:

1. RATIFICATION OF SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The subscription, allotment, and payment of [X] common shares at par value of KRW [Y] per share, resulting in paid-in capital of KRW [Z], is in all respects ratified, confirmed, and approved. The directors are directed to issue share certificates, record shareholders in the registry, and file any capital increase or reduction documentation required by Korean law.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is hereby adopted at [registered office address]. The Chief Executive Officer and the Company Secretary are authorized to execute the lease, register the address, and carry out all administrative steps necessary for the registered office.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. [Bank Name] at [branch address] is authorized to accept and operate one or more corporate current, foreign currency, and segregated trust accounts in the name of the Company. Any two of the representative director, chief financial officer, and treasurer shall sign and deliver checks, wire transfer instructions, SWIFT instructions, and escrow release instructions, except where the representative director acts alone for deposits only.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and co-representative director; [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; and [Name] is appointed statutory auditor, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting and to be registered with the relevant court registry.

5. CERTIFICATION AND ADMINISTRATION. The representatives are authorized to certify this resolution, file with the registration office, bank, tax office and stock exchange, and to procure legal counsel to take all necessary actions to fulfill the mandatory corporate governance and escrow requirements.

ADOPTED this [date] by unanimous consent of the directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Initial Organizational Acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Panel, Civil Affairs Bureau, Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators shall prepare the Articles of Incorporation in compliance with Commercial Act Articles 289 and 292, stating the corporate purpose as a Special Purpose Acquisition Company qualified to acquire one or more domestic or overseas businesses after listing. The Articles shall state the total authorized shares, par value, initial subscription shares, method of contribution, and limited-purpose operating restrictions. All incorporators or their lawful agents must personally attend the notary public and affirm incorporation intent. The notary shall certify the Articles and record the date of notarization. Thereafter, the incorporators must cause all subscription amounts to be deposited into a provisional bank account opened in the name of the promoters or corporation, and obtain the bank payment certificate required by Article 291 of the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Notarial certificate draft
Identity documents and power of attorney for each incorporator
Certificate of share subscription determination
Bank payment certificate for subscription amount deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a correction notice, the incorporators shall amend the defective clauses, obtain new share subscription resolutions, re-notarize, and pay additional notarial fees before proceeding to court registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court Registration Office or the District Court Registration Office with jurisdiction over the principal place of business
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks of payment or capital deposit, the incorporators or statutory representatives shall file an application for incorporation registration under Commercial Act Article 317 with the registration office of the principal office location. The application shall list the SPAC purpose, issued and paid-in shares, paid-in capital amount, address of the registered office, name and identity of directors, statutory auditor or audit committee member, and representative directors. The court shall review the notarized Articles, payment certificates, directors' election and acceptance documents, and appendices. Upon approval, the court will enter the company in the corporate registry and issue a corporate registration certificate and a corporate seal certificate, enabling further tax and financial licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Application for Stock Company Incorporation Registration
Bank certificate proving full payment of subscription price
Acceptance letters of directors, representative directors and statutory auditor
Proof of identity and authority of incorporators
Notice of selection of corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court returns the application for correction, the applicant shall file an amendment within the stated cure period, remedy the cause of rejection, and pay any revised court registration fees; failure to cure may cause the filing to be deemed withdrawn and require a fresh submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business and Tax Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic portal, supervised by the local District Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty business days after court registration, the Company shall complete business registration under the Framework Act on Taxation to obtain a Business Registration Certificate. The application must select the business type appropriate to a financial services holding vehicle or SPAC and use the corporate registration number. The Company must disclose its registered office lease, corporate seal certificate, Articles and register, and identity documents. If the Company opens a corporate bank account, the Business Registration Certificate must be presented to the bank under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. The National Tax Service will issue the certificate after verifying the principal place of business through the assigned tax office.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate
Certified copies of Articles of Incorporation and board resolutions
Business registration application form
Registered office lease contract
Corporate seal certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service sends a demand for correction or requests further information, the Company shall correct administrative errors, update the business purpose code on the electronic filing system, and resubmit the application to the local district tax office before statutory deadlines expire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Officer Appointments, Banking Authorization and Trust Escrow Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial banks and securities firms authorized under the Banking Act and Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; National Tax Service for tax account integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation, the directors shall convene the First Board of Directors meeting to adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution. The board shall appoint statutory officers, adopt the registered office address, and authorize the opening of current, foreign currency and trust escrow accounts. The Company shall execute a custodian or trust agreement with a licensed securities firm or trustee bank for the purpose of segregating SPAC IPO proceeds as separately managed funds, satisfying Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act Article 180 and the Korea Exchange KOSDAQ listing requirements. The bank shall verify the representative director's identity, corporate seal, Business Registration Certificate, and the board resolution. Upon verification, account numbers and SWIFT payment instructions will be delivered to the Company.
required_dossiers: Pro-Forma First Board Resolution
Corporate seal certificate and corporate certificate of registration
Business registration certificate
Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of representative directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to unresolved know-your-customer, corporate authority, or document deficiencies, the board must cure the identified defects, provide an updated corporate register, or apply to another licensed Korean bank; if the trust escrow documentation is rejected by the Korea Exchange, a revised trust agreement must be resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SPAC Regulatory Filing and KOSDAQ Listing Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission, Financial Supervisory Service, and Korea Exchange KOSDAQ Market Disclosure and Listing Review Divisions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: As a Special Purpose Acquisition Company, the Company must prepare and file a securities registration statement with the Financial Supervisory Service and simultaneously file a preliminary listing review application with Korea Exchange KOSDAQ. The filing must evidence that paid-in capital is no less than KRW 3,000,000,000 and that at least 90 percent of the gross offering proceeds are deposited into the independent trust escrow account. The Company must also file its corporate charter, Articles, board resolutions, financial statements, auditor reports, sponsor agreement and underwriter commitment letter. After the Financial Services Commission accepts the registration statement and the Korea Exchange approves the preliminary listing review, the Company may issue its final prospectus and proceed to public listing, subject to any amendments required by the regulators.
required_dossiers: Securities registration statement and SPAC prospectus
Trust escrow agreement and proof of deposit
Financial statements and auditor's report
Sponsor agreement and underwriter commitment letter
Articles of Incorporation and corporate governance charter
KOSDAQ preliminary listing review application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Financial Services Commission issues a document review comment or preliminary rejection, the Company shall respond within the prescribed period, generally ten to fifteen business days, by amending the registration statement, correcting misleading disclosures, and refiling with the Financial Supervisory Service; if Korea Exchange questions SPAC eligibility, the Company shall submit a written supplement and additional evidence of escrow and capital compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission, Financial Supervisory Service, and Korea Exchange KOSDAQ Market; Ministry of Employment and Labor for general office occupational safety only if employees are engaged
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Securities Registration Statement for SPAC Common Stock and KOSDAQ Listing Authorization pursuant to the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; no separate physical industrial operating permit is required for a non-manufacturing financial blank-check vehicle.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, Environmental Impact Assessment Division, together with relevant local environmental authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt and Not Applicable. ISIC 6499 SPAC is a non-manufacturing, non-chemical, non-assembly financial vehicle with no construction of physical industrial facilities and no site operations requiring a Full EIA Report or an Environmental Registration under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The Company has no process wastewater discharge points, VOC emission stacks, stationary combustion sources, or hazardous waste generation points. If the Company later acquires and physically operates an industrial target company, a fresh EIA classification and all quantitative discharge, emissions, and waste handling standards applicable to the target's actual ISIC code shall be assessed at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to the SPAC itself because it does not conduct physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. If the Company maintains a registered office or sponsor office with employees, it must comply with the Fire-Fighting System Installation and Safety Control Act, obtain the applicable fire safety certificate for the premises, satisfy structural load standards under the Building Act, and comply with the Korean Occupational Safety and Health Act administered by the Ministry of Employment and Labor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, administered through the HomeTax online electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); export and customs procedures are executed with the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS single-window system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa incorporated under the Korean Commercial Act, the statutory TIN procedure is as follows: (1) complete incorporation and court registration; (2) submit the foreign investment notification, if applicable, to KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; (3) within 20 days from business commencement, submit the Application for Business Registration to the competent district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office; (4) attach the certificate of corporate registration, articles of incorporation, proof of domestic business premises, authenticated shareholder identification (apostilled or consular-legalized for foreign shareholders), and the foreign investment notification certificate; and (5) obtain the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the national TIN and, after VAT activation, as the HomeTax VAT ID. A foreign non-resident entity without a domestic place of business that realizes Korean-source income must instead register through the HomeTax portal, obtain a non-resident TIN, and appoint a domestic tax representative with a power of attorney under Article 82 of the Framework Act on National Taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean law does not provide a check-the-box or elective pass-through regime for domestic corporations; a Chusik Hoesa is a domestic resident corporation taxed on worldwide income at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act. Cross-border hybrid arrangements are instead constrained by the Hybrid Mismatch Arrangement rules in the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs and the OECD BEPS Action 2 recommendations, which disallow deduction/non-inclusion mismatches and require conformity with the place-of-effective-management tests.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) pursuant to the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No exemption threshold exists: every person who commences a taxable business must apply for VAT registration with the competent district tax office within 20 days under Article 53 of the Value-Added Tax Act, regardless of turnover. Simplified taxpayers with annual taxable supplies of KRW 80 million or less may apply simplified turnover-based assessment but remain mandatorily registered. A newly formed special purpose acquisition company must therefore register immediately even if its escrow/trust interest income is VAT-exempt financial income.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoicing for all B2B supplies. Every registered business must issue electronic tax invoices (ETIs) via the NTS HomeTax national e-invoicing infrastructure and transmit the ETI data to the NTS using the integrated XML/API and G2B/EDI interfaces within the statutory issuance deadline (transaction-based ETIs by the next day following the date of supply; monthly aggregated ETIs no later than the 15th day of the month following the supply month). The NTS validates transmitted invoices in near real time, assigns a national electronic invoice number, performs anti-fraud digital attestation, and may flag abnormal issuers; delayed or omitted transmission triggers automated notices and statutory addition taxes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods qualify for a 0% rate if they are physically removed from Korea under a valid customs export declaration made in UNI-PASS. Cross-border services (services performed for non-residents outside the Korean territory, international transportation and overseas construction/technical services under foreign-exchange earning contracts) also qualify when the customer and place of supply are outside Korea. For a Chusik Hoesa, any cross-border investment-advisory or M&A service will be zero-rated only if it satisfies the foreign service/foreign-exchange earning contract tests and is supported by remittance of proceeds from abroad; domestic escrow interest and domestic listing fees remain VAT-exempt or taxable, not zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Certificate (export customs clearance certificate) issued by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS single window
Ocean Bill of Lading or Airway Bill naming the Korean exporter as shipper (or a recognized freight forwarder cargo receipt)
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate / inward remittance credit advice from a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing collection of export proceeds
Underlying sale or purchase contract (and, for service exports, a foreign exchange earning contract) showing the foreign counterparty, service description, and payment terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are cross-matched by the NTS and Korea Customs Service against UNI-PASS export declarations, cargo manifests, bank foreign exchange settlement records, and HomeTax filings. If any required document is missing, forged, or inconsistent, the NTS retroactively assesses 10% output VAT on the gross supply value, disallows related input VAT credits/refunds, and imposes addition taxes of up to 40% of the unpaid VAT (with aggravated treatment and extended 10-year statute of limitations for fraudulent claims) plus daily late-payment interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Willful fraudulent zero-rating also triggers criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (imprisonment up to 3 years or fines up to KRW 30 million, with aggravated penalties up to 10 years for large-scale evasion), and the NTS may suspend the offending entity's electronic tax invoice transmission privileges and export refund eligibility.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized yet regulated foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions, including ordinary trade settlements, service payments, and dividend remittances, are generally freely convertible subject to reporting and supporting documentation. Capital account transactions, such as equity injections, loan borrowings, and proceeds from SPAC initial public offerings, require prior notification or approval under the FETA, with submission through a designated Foreign Exchange Bank. The Korean won does not enjoy offshore convertibility; won must be exchanged domestically. Export proceeds do not face a rigid mandatory surrender ratio under the current regime, but exporters must settle or repatriate receipts within statutory timelines and provide valuation evidence to the receiving bank. Profit remittance hurdles include Corporate Income Tax certificate issuance, audited financial statements, proof of shareholding registry, and confirmation that the remitted amount corresponds to distributable earnings. For a SPAC vehicle, inbound capital earmarked for escrow or IPO proceeds requires a capital verification report certified by an independent licensed CPA and may be subject to MOEF reporting if the transaction exceeds threshold amounts. Cross-border transfers above KRW 500 million require a general report; while those with legal or financial substance above KRW 5 billion might require the approval of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Committee. The overall environment permits legal incorporation and repatriation, but the bank must document each movement using purpose codes and maintain an audit trail for BOK inspection for at least five years.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must receive export proceeds within 18 months from the date of the export declaration (export license date). If the exporter maintains a foreign currency deposit account, the proceeds may remain in that account without immediate conversion; however, any conversion into KRW must be executed through a Foreign Exchange Bank. There is no mandatory percentage surrender requirement; the statutory default is full retention in foreign currency or full conversion at the exporter's election, subject to FETA reporting obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: SPAC Capital Escrow Account and Operational KRW Account
SPAC Capital Escrow Account and Corporate FX Settlement Account
SPAC Management Trust Account and Operating Currency Account
Escrow Trust Account and Multi-currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs and virtual bank challengers are not legally permitted to open or maintain current or escrow accounts for Korean incorporated entities unless they hold a license under the Banking Act or the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. A foreign-imposed EMI, such as those chartered in the EEA or Singapore, cannot service Korean domiciled SPAC operations without a domestic branch and FSS authorization. As a result, fintech EMI viability is rated Low for treasury clearing and Medium only as auxiliary payment channels for domestic disbursements if they partner with tier-1 licensed Korean banks. The SPAC's investor-facing escrow, IPO underwriting, and custodial functions must be domiciled at a Korean commercial bank or a licensed trust company to satisfy FSC regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory directors of the Korean SPAC are required to complete in-branch identity verification or, under bank-specific digital onboarding frameworks, to conduct a live supervisory video interview with the compliance officer. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted only for non-resident beneficial owners and for foreign signatories who hold a power of attorney notarized at the local Korean embassy or consulate; however, at least one standing director domiciled in Korea must appear physically or through an equivalent video appointment at a local branch. The bank will reject simple courier or digital selfie KYC for a medium-risk enhanced SPAC classification without a licensed legal or financial intermediary jointly filing the opening documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SPAC blank-check vehicle with opaque beneficial ownership or high-risk IP address origin from secrecy jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Beneficial Ownership Extract (not older than 6 months) from the Korean Court Registry (Jungdeungso); detailed corporate tree showing every beneficial owner above 10% with passport copies and national ID validation; a FATCA/CRS self-certification form for each owner; an sworn affidavit from the SPAC CEO describing the source of underwriting capital; and a legal opinion from a Korean licensed attorney confirming no shell, nominee, or straw-principal structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection exceeding KRW 500 million from foreign investors without clear source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Investment Trust Deed; bank statements for the last 6 months of each wiring entity; accountant-certified statements proving lawful accumulation of wealth (salary, dividends, property sale, or inheritance); Foreign Exchange Banking Report form 1-B with purpose code 6010; notarised board resolution of the SPAC authorizing capital inflow; and an independently audited Capital Verification Report issued by a licensed Korean external auditor verifying the receipt and the legal permissibility of the funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow account instructions inconsistent with the IPO prospectus or trust agreement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Final FSS-approved securities registration statement (draft or effective); executed Trust Agreement with the domestic licensed custodian; a side-by-side schedule mapping each investor payment into the escrow sub-ledger; the underwriter's capital collection account reconciliation; and a legal affirmation that no portion of the escrow funds is to be used before merger or business completion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected round-tripping or intra-group lending disguised as operating revenue or capital contribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated financial statements of the ultimate parent; proof of arm's length valuation of any transferred crypto assets or intangible licences; a transfer pricing opinion from a Big Four auditor confirming fair market value; and a statement from the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank confirming the transaction was filed under the correct purpose code and was not segmented to avoid review thresholds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Korean SPAC must be routed through a designated Foreign Exchange Bank using SWIFT MT103 messages with exact Korean Won settlement instructions. The remitter must include a clear reference to the SPAC investment contract and the unique KOLAS business registration number. The bank will escrow funds in a segregated custody account if required by the FSC, and the SPAC must submit the capital verification report from its statutory auditor within 30 days to complete the Foreign Exchange Reporting requirement. The correct FETA purpose code for equity capital is 6010. For acquisition funding to be used after a merger, the routing must also include a copy of the board resolution and the FSC-registered business combination disclosure. The bank will release the funds to operating accounts only after the capital verification and anti-money laundering reconciliation are completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements related to post-merger acquisition targets, the preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 wire through the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank for direct supplier payments. For large or documentary transactions, commercial Letters of Credit are advised with the Korean bank as the issuing bank under UCP 600; documentary collections and trade receivables may also be routed through B2B interbank channels. All outbound disbursements require a valid underlying contract, a confirmed FETA purpose code (e.g., 9110 for service or 3100 for imports), and an adverse media screening record. For SPAC-related advisory fees or merger costs, the bank will require an invoice, the executed service agreement, and evidence that the payee is not a sanctioned entity or jurisdiction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts for KRW/USD and KRW/JPY with a physical delivery obligation, permitted only for hedgers with underlying current or capital exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for KRW may be executed offshore or domestically only with BOK-approved counterparties, typically central banks or licensed global banks; retail SPAC vehicles are not eligible
Cross-currency swaps are permitted when the underlying exposure is a formalised foreign currency debt or future acquisition payment backed by executed contracts
Options and exotic derivatives are restricted; simple vanilla swaps and forwards are permissible if the notional amount does not exceed the documented exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Law, Article 60)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) or the governing District Tax Office via the NTS HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the 3rd month following fiscal year-end (31 March for a 31 December year-end); with an audit report or tax-adjustment statement prepared by a Korean tax accountant, the deadline is extended by one month to 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: NTS estimated assessment for non-filing; non-filing penalty of 20% of the assessed tax; negligent under-reporting penalty of 10% and 0.022% daily arrears interest per day of unpaid tax; prolonged non-compliance permits the NTS to classify the company as dormant, cancel the business registration, and initiate administrative strike-off/winding-up

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and the Audited Financial Statements (Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Article 4)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) as the audit-report repository, with simultaneous filing of the audited statements to the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 March of the following year, before the deadline for the annual shareholders' meeting; the registered CPA must submit the audit report to the FSS within the period determined by the external audit regulations after the audit completion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or submit an audit report triggers administrative fines under the External Audit Act and may cause the FSS to designate a statutory auditor; the unresolved audit deficiency is reported to the registry and may prevent lawful shareholder approval, ultimately leading to an administrative wind-up proceeding for non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report for Listed Companies (Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, Article 159)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system; and to Korea Exchange (KRX) for listed-company public disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (31 March for a 31 December SPAC), including the audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: KRX may impose disclosure corrective measures, issue a public warning, suspend trading, or delist the SPAC; the FSCMA imposes criminal fines up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment for deliberately false or omitted annual report disclosure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external payment or filing fee; statutory records and minutes are retained at the registered office. Any changes made at the AGM that affect directors, auditors, or capital are registered with the Commercial Registration Office of the local District Court.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the fiscal year-end, i.e. by 31 March for a December fiscal year; convening notice must be dispatched at least 14 days before the meeting (Article 363 Korean Commercial Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Repeated failure to convene exposes each responsible director to administrative fines up to KRW 5 million; shareholders may request a court order to summon an extraordinary shareholders' meeting; failure to approve financial statements while maintaining operating status can lead to business closure and involuntary dissolution by court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Local Surtax (Inhabitant Tax) Annual Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: City, County, or District Local Government Tax Office (WeTax local tax e-filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-year annual filing due simultaneously with the corporate income tax return: 31 March, with the same 30 April extension when the tax basis is audited
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax authority adds a 20% non-filing penalty on the surtax plus daily arrears interest; severe delinquency allows arrest of bank accounts and cancellation of the business registration certificate, leading to strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Korean Chusik Hoesa formed as a SPAC is unconditionally subject to independent audit because it is a listed public company under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, regardless of balance sheet, revenue, or headcount. For a non-listed stock corporation, mandatory external audit applies under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if the total assets immediately before the preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 10 billion, or if designated by the Financial Services Commission as a public-interest company, or if it meets the Presidential Decree threshold (including certain companies with assets of KRW 5 billion or more and high revenue or headcount, and companies with financial-institution status). A SPAC holding IPO trust proceeds also meets the audit-mandatory category irrespective of the size of its liquid assets.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as endorsed by the Korea Accounting Standards Board is mandatory for the listed SPAC's consolidated and separate financial statements. Unlisted companies not qualifying for K-IFRS may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) or the Small and Medium Enterprise Accounting Standards, but the

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income tax surcharge, producing an aggregate top marginal burden of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified foreign-invested corporations may access Restriction of Special Taxation Act incentives, including 5-year 100% corporate tax exemption and 50% reduction for the following 2 years in designated Free Economic Zones; R&D tax credits up to 50% of qualifying expenditures; temporary investment tax credits; and extended loss carryforward relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, with semi-annual interim prepayment filings
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year, i.e. by 31 March for calendar-year-end SPACs; interim prepayment returns are due within 3 months after the end of the first 6 months of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Business Registration Number, fiscal-year opening and closing dates, head office address, representative director name, and industry classification as ISIC 6499 blank-check acquisition company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean head-office and management address exactly as registered. If the SPAC is non-resident-managed or its tax residency is challenged, attach a tax-treaty tiebreaker analysis and evidence that central management and control are exercised in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Taxable Income and Global Income Scope
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of worldwide taxable income after statutory adjustments under the Corporate Tax Act, including SPAC trust and escrow account earnings, non-deductible expenses, exempt income, and loss deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest and trust fund income from escrow and M&A deposit accounts is taxable if the Korean SPAC is the legal earner. Non-resident shareholders cannot declare this income on their own Korean returns; the entity must tax it before any distribution to foreign investors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Non-Resident Shareholder and Beneficial Ownership Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all non-resident shareholders, shareholding percentages, country of residence, ultimate beneficial owners, and any indirect foreign ownership chains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident shareholder, attach a current Tax Residency Certificate and Beneficial Owner Declaration. Failure to disclose a controlling foreign parent or a foreign SPAC cascade activates Korean Controlled Foreign Corporation rules under the Korean International Tax Adjustment Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Corporate Tax Computation, Rates, and Local Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Progressive national corporate income tax computation under Corporate Tax Act Article 55, followed by the 10% local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents do not claim their home-country tax credit on this line. The Korean SPAC must verify that no prohibited deferred compensation, sham financing, or artificial interest stripping has reduced the Korean tax base below the statutory rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - International Transactions and Transfer Pricing Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed records of cross-border related-party transactions, intercompany fees, management charges, interest accruals, royalty payments, and functional, asset, and risk analyses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If aggregate foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion, append Local File and Master File before filing. Non-arm's length charges to the Korean SPAC will be adjusted upward, increasing Korean taxable income and triggering additional penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Withholding Tax on Remittances to Non-Resident Shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation and settlement of final withholding tax on dividend distributions, interest payments, and royalty payments made to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter each foreign recipient, DTA rate, Tax Residency Certificate reference, and beneficial ownership status. Without a valid treaty relief application, a 22% aggregate withholding obligation applies and the Korean paying SPAC remains statutorily liable as withholding agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and unfaithful-report penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes include 20% of unpaid tax for non-filing, 10% for under-reporting, and 40% for fraudulent understatement, plus overdue daily interest at 0.022%. Chronic non-filers can be publicly registered, denied tax clearance certificates, subjected to departure restrictions, and criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate, comprising 20% national corporate income tax withholding on dividends under Corporate Tax Act Article 98 plus 2% local income tax surcharge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident recipient must file an Application for Tax Treaty Reduction or Exemption of Withholding Tax before the dividend payment, through HomeTax or the competent district tax office, attaching a Tax Residency Certificate, a Beneficial Owner Declaration, share ownership records, and evidence that the recipient is not a treaty-shopping conduit. The Korean withholding agent must preserve these records for at least six years; excess withheld tax may be recovered through a refund claim filed within the statutory limitation period, ordinarily three years from the date the overpayment becomes final.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory aggregate rate of 22% applies to outbound interest and royalties absent treaty relief, comprising 20% national tax and 2% local surcharge. Approved bilateral DTA rates generally reduce interest to 10-15% and royalties to 10-15%, subject to limitations-on-benefits provisions, beneficial ownership requirements, and demonstrable economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate cross-border related-party transactions per fiscal year triggers mandatory Master File and Local File preparation and submission with or upon request during the tax audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies economic substance concepts through the Korean International Tax Adjustment Act general anti-avoidance rule, Controlled Foreign Corporation provisions, tax treaty beneficial-ownership rules, and anti-artificial transaction doctrine. A SPAC must maintain board meetings in Korea, strategic M&A target identification, escrow and trust account management from Korea, actual office facilities, and substantive staff payroll; failure to do so can result in recharacterization as a sham, denial of DTA relief, and CFC income attribution to controlling shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of trust or escrow interest income, false documentation of non-resident ownership, and deliberate under-declaration of the SPAC's taxable income for the benefit of foreign shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 imposes imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of up to five times the evaded national and local tax; additional 40% fraud penalty is imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and the corporation may be publicly disclosed as a chronic tax defaulter.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns face piercing of the corporate veil through joint and several civil liability for underpaid tax and interest, National Tax Service blacklisting with travel bans, refusal of tax clearance certificates, and criminal imprisonment for up to five years in aggravated fraudulent evasion cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty-Shopping Abuse Without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean SPAC as a mailing-address-only shell with no office, employees, economic assets, or substantive management decisions in Korea, while claiming DTA benefits on outbound distributions or attempting to defer Korean tax through a foreign conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korean International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 2 and 17 authorize recharacterization, constructive dividend treatment, and denial of treaty benefits; Framework Act on National Taxes adds fraudulent and negligent surcharges, and Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act sanctions apply for false disclosures in a SPAC listing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under Commercial Act Articles 399 and 401 for damages caused to the corporation and third parties, separately assessed for unpaid tax, barred from future SPAC directorships, and subject to imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act if the shell structure is used to commit tax fraud, together with travel restrictions and asset freezing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Foreign Exchange and SPAC Registration Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving acquisition funds through unlicensed offshore escrow accounts, operating a multi-tier SPAC to conceal beneficial owners, or failing to report Korean foreign financial accounts when the balance exceeds KRW 500 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Article 137 imposes imprisonment for up to 3 years or a fine of up to KRW 100 million; the Act on Reporting and Using Certain Financial Transaction Information imposes sanctions on designated non-financial businesses for failing to identify beneficial owners, including fines of up to KRW 50 million per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers and representative directors can be criminally arrested and detained, personal assets may be frozen in civil restitution actions, and immigration blacklisting may be imposed by the authorities, leading to travel bans and disqualification from managing regulated financial entities.
